author: Astra

target.identity_scope: BCM4378 is the selected target family for this plan. These three generic driver files contain BCM4378 support, but do not associate J293 with a measured chip revision, OTP module, antenna SKU or firmware board suffix. This task performed no device observation.
target.PCI_match: pcie.c includes BRCM_PCIE_4378_DEVICE_ID with WCC_SEED driver data. Its numeric PCI device-ID constant is in an excluded header, so no numeric value is claimed from these three files.

source_boundary.method: Read these existing local bytes as reference data; independently rechecked length, SHA256 and Git blob ID. The note paraphrases behavior and reproduces no Linux implementation.

firmware_selection.unsupported_revision: BCM4378 revision4 matches neither row. firmware.c rejects revisions>=32 before shifting. Do not round an unknown revision to B1/B3.
firmware_selection.reference_directory_prefix: BRCMF_FW_DEFAULT_PATH is used, but its definition is in an excluded header. This three-file note establishes filename stems/extensions, not a fully expanded directory prefix.

roles..bin: Wi-Fi firmware executable; required by this request.
roles..txt: Board NVRAM/calibration text; optional in the Linux request API, not evidence that arbitrary or absent calibration is suitable for J293.
roles..clm_blob: Regulatory/country-locale payload retained for later common-driver use.
roles..txcap_blob: Transmit-capability payload retained for later common-driver use.
roles..sig: Optional signature information used when constructing firmware footers.

firmware_selection.reference_optionality: pcie.c marks NVRAM, CLM, TXCAP and signature optional; executable binary is mandatory. Missing optional files do not make radio operation, regulation or board calibration correct. Functions consuming CLM/TXCAP after the bus is up are outside these three files.
firmware_selection.board_path_rule: Insert the chosen board qualifier between the firmware stem and its extension, try the ordered qualifiers, then the canonical stem+extension. With no complete Apple OTP/settings tuple, only the supplied board_type qualifier is used. No model-to-board_type derivation is present here.
firmware_selection.OTP_source: For BCM4378 the reference selects the GCI core OTP shadow at core-relative0x1120 and reads0x170 little16-bit words. It parses bounded vendor tuples for module/vendor/version. Selecting that shadow requires a PCI BAR-window config write; it is not a passive PCI-config-only observation.
firmware_selection.actual_J293_suffix: UNKNOWN in this task. The Apple-qualified name in a source comment is an example, not a J293 selection or permitted substitute.
firmware_selection.content_policy: No firmware, signature, regulatory/calibration blob or OTP data was read, downloaded, copied, redistributed or manufactured. A future native loader needs explicit artifact provenance, actual chip revision and board identity.

reference_bringup_sequence.behavior: Match the supported PCI function, allocate per-device state, and call chip attach through bus operations. The PCI prepare operation enables the device, enables bus mastering, obtains/maps the register BAR and TCM memory BAR, and rejects missing resources. This presumes host bridge, power/link and DMA isolation already exist.

reference_bringup_sequence.phase: Chip/backplane recognition and passive CPU state
reference_bringup_sequence.behavior: Read ChipCommon chip/revision and bus type through the selected BAR window. Enumerate the supported backplane/core directory, check required cores, halt/reset the embedded CPU, perform the bus reset hook and re-establish passive state. Discover RAM geometry and chip capabilities. The BCM4378 RAM-base case is0x352000; size still comes from discovered hardware/firmware information. Chip attach therefore writes/reset hardware and cannot be reused as a read-only probe.

Select register layout from PCIe-core revision. Establish per-device bus/protocol ownership and vendor settings, read/parse OTP for the WCC path, then select the exact chip-revision stem and Apple board-qualified alternatives. BCM4378 uses the WCC seed-enabled row, so later firmware handoff may include a fresh random seed.

reference_bringup_sequence.phase: Validate firmware inputs and prepare interrupts
reference_bringup_sequence.behavior: Asynchronously acquire the executable and selected optional inputs. Parse board NVRAM into the firmware representation: select the appropriate per-device subset when present, remove irrelevant text, preserve/add the reference defaults and authorized platform MAC, NUL/pad to four bytes and append the word-count/complement token. Refresh RAM information and inspect any recognized firmware RAM-size trailer. Prepare the firmware-boot interrupt path before starting the embedded CPU.

reference_bringup_sequence.phase: Download and start embedded Wi-Fi firmware
reference_bringup_sequence.behavior: Enter download state with mailbox/host IRQ sources masked and acknowledged. Copy the executable into device TCM, retain its first word as the reset entry, place selected NVRAM and any seed/signature/footer data at the top of bounded device RAM, and clear the shared-RAM startup marker. Release the CPU through its discovered core implementation. Poll the marker in50ms steps for at most5s; reject timeout or a shared pointer outside device RAM. This is real device execution, not a discovery operation.

Validate firmware shared-memory protocol version and capability flags; obtain mailbox/ring metadata and index widths. Allocate and publish common/flow-ring and scratch/update DMA buffers, preserving their backing. Only then attach the common FullMAC stack. The source uses MSGBUF, not a generic Ethernet-register interface; association, security, country/regulatory control and packet policy require additional components absent from this three-file subset.

Preserve the original error, stop new bus activity, disable and synchronize interrupts, cancel reset work, detach the upper protocol, stop/reset device activity and release DMA/rings, mappings and references under explicit ownership. The Linux sequence is a behavioral reference, not proof of Darwin callback/DMA quiescence. A Darwin adapter must retain any backing whose device access cannot yet be proven stopped.

smallest_original_Darwin_slice.proposed_name: PDBCM4378Identity + portable4378 firmware-selection policy, proposed only
smallest_original_Darwin_slice.scope: An opt-in diagnostic IOService on an already enumerated, independently owned IOPCIDevice, plus original pure-C chip/revision/filename and bounded OTP-tuple decoders. No network interface registration and no claim of packets, scanning or association.
first_outputs: Exact enumerated vendor/device/subsystem/revision identity from existing PCI config access
Existing BAR resource ranges and ownership/readiness status, without resize/probe writes
BCM4378 chip-revision firmware plan from explicitly supplied/validated chip identity and board metadata; unknown values remain unknown
Finite numeric stage/result and input provenance, without serial/OTP/MAC data in public logs
smallest_original_Darwin_slice.first_hardware_boundary: Do not call or mimic the full Linux chip_attach just to identify a device. Start with no PCI Command/BAR-window/core/reset write and no bus-master enable. A later bounded ChipCommon/EROM identity transaction needs a separate host-bridge/resource lease covering its necessary BAR-window selection writes and rollback; do not invent an all-read-only access path.
admission_requirements: PCI host/link/power and endpoint ownership supplied by the lead platform work; these three files do not implement T8103 host bring-up
Real DART/IOMapper and DMA/invalidation/quiescence contract before bus mastering or publishing any DMA address
Correct ARM64 interrupt/MSI ownership before an executable firmware start; no x86 fallback inferred
Actual chip revision, board type, antenna SKU and permitted firmware/calibration provenance before a filename becomes a loader decision
pure_host_tests: Board-qualified fallback order and extension insertion; bounded strings and rejection of unsafe path components
Truncated/overflowing OTP tuples, absent module/vendor/version and no use of partially parsed identity
NVRAM/token construction and firmware/RAM interval-overlap arithmetic on synthetic data only
Failure before ownership leaves PCI/MMIO/DMA callbacks untouched; async completion cannot outlive its per-device owner
later_slices: Owned backplane identity/RAM discovery with bounded transactions and explicit mutation journal
Approved firmware download plus independently contained boot-ready interrupt/shared-memory handshake
Original MSGBUF ring/control/data protocol and IONetworkingFamily integration after DMA ownership is genuine
smallest_original_Darwin_slice.failure_policy: Missing bridge, power, identity, IRQ, mapper or firmware input yields explicit NOT_READY/UNSUPPORTED. Do not fabricate a live interface, successful firmware start or Wi-Fi association.

limits_of_three_file_reference: The J293 board-to-firmware qualifier mapping, numeric header-defined PCI IDs/register masks, PMGR/SMC/PERST/PCI host setup, DART/RID-SID policy and Darwin network APIs are outside this allowed source set.
Common MSGBUF/FullMAC/cfg80211 protocol implementations, CLM/TXCAP application and radio regulation/association are called here but not implemented by these three files.
No measured chip revision, OTP identity or real firmware-byte compatibility was established. The BCM4388-specific42-bit DMA workaround is not evidence for BCM4378.
unchanged_boundaries: Lead Codex goal and network-link files
